title: Machine learning-based survival modeling reveals distinct surgical benefits across molecular subtypes in young women with de novo metastatic breast cancer
summary: Machine-learning survival analyses in young women with de novo metastatic breast cancer identified molecular-subtype differences in observed surgical-benefit associations; this is retrospective treatment-effect modeling, not causal proof.
ai_technology: Machine-learning survival models stratified by breast-cancer molecular subtype
organization: Affiliation not stated in the reviewed material

evidence.tested: The retrospective survival analysis compares observed surgical-benefit associations across molecular subtypes in young women with de novo metastatic breast cancer; it does not establish causal benefit.
evidence.unknown: The subtype-specific treatment associations are retrospective and do not establish a causal benefit from surgery.
evidence.ai_role: Uses survival modeling stratified by molecular subtype to compare observed surgical-benefit associations in young women with de novo metastatic breast cancer.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
